Both inputs read in full, plus the path/tier checks needed to make the manifest real. Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land.

---

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, now 20 commits** (18 originally; the
> 3.5 stepper-wiring insertion on 2026-09-18 made it 19, the 4.6 cartDrawerContainer insertion on
> 2026-09-20 made it 20 — this line and the other plain "18"/"eighteen" mentions below went stale
> both times and were only just corrected; treat this number as the one to keep current, not
> re-derive from memory, if a further step ever gets inserted).
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

### B0 — e2e area

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml` | modify | **Tier 1 CI/CD** | `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` |

> **BLOCKED.** Named explicitly in the brief, but owner approval is not confirmed. Per Hard Rule #2 the Implementer must either verify the authenticated `gh` login is in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (`gh api user --jq .login`, then the team membership call) or stop and get a named approving review before touching it. Do not start B0 on an unverified session.

Add a `cart` group to `detect-changes`'s allow-lists covering `overrides/app/pages/cart/**`, `overrides/app/components/product-item/**`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/**`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*/**`, `e2e/tests/zimm/cart/**`, `e2e/features/cart/**`. Note `e2e_homepage` is currently the **only** area group in the file — `testing.md`'s longer tag list is aspirational, so `cart` is the second, not the eighth.

### B1 — SFCC-315

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.test.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.stories.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.ts` | create | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` | **modify** | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` | modify | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | modify | **Tier 2** | `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers` |

### B2 — SFCC-270 (copy-first)

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

548	## 5. Loop configuration
549	
550	**Read `## 5.0 Verification standard` (added 2026-09-19, right after this table) before running
551	any of the remaining rows (3.6 onward).** It's a cross-cutting addition earned the hard way during
552	the post-commit-11 ad hoc pass — six real, shipped defects slipped past this table's own
553	per-step checks the first time through, all for the same handful of reasons. The per-step checks
554	below are unchanged and still the specific thing being tested; §5.0 is what makes sure they're
555	actually being *proven*, not just read off the source and assumed.
556	
557	| Step | Tester checks | Scorer PASS gate |
558	|---|---|---|
559	| **0** | Nothing to drive. Read `detect-changes`'s output on the first cart PR after merge. | `e2e_scope == cart` on a cart-only PR; `homepage` still resolves for a homepage-only PR; zero-spec `--grep "@cart"` run reports "no tests found" and exits 0. |
560	| **1.1** | Resolve `xLarge` at 1440 and 1920 viewport widths. Confirm 1186px both times, not 1180.8 and 1574. Confirm the five other size variants byte-identical. | 1186px rem constant at both widths; `maxWidth: '100%'` present; five sibling variants unchanged; `grep` for `xLarge` consumers still returns only the type union and the story. |
561	| **1.2** | Drive the drawer: open, Escape, backdrop click, close button. Tab through and confirm focus never escapes the panel. Close and confirm focus returns to the trigger **and** scroll position is where it was. Render empty and confirm the 52px band is still occupying space. Resize 1920 → 1440 → 834 → 402 and confirm two-column → single-column at tablet with a 32px gutter. | All four close paths call `onClose`; `finalFocusRef` receives focus; scroll offset restored (not just unlocked); `min-height` on the messages band equals the 52px token in the empty story; single-column at and below tablet; `659.2` appears nowhere; `recipeParts` and `recipeGuards` green; recipe registered. |
562	| **2.1** | This is the one step the Tester cannot score alone. Confirm all eight markers log in the running app **from three surfaces**: the cart, the account wishlist page, and a checkout summary. | Eight files, `.tsx`, `tsc` clean, zero logic diff from base, `item-variant` imports relative not base-path, markers observed on all three surfaces, **Marcel's explicit go-ahead recorded** before step 2.2 starts. |
563	| **2.2** | Pass a `width` and an `mr` to `CartItemVariantImage` from a test caller and confirm the caller wins. Pass a `color` to `CartItemVariantName` and confirm it applies. Render with no stepper and no actions. Render at 402px and look for any truncation or hidden element. | Caller-props win on image and name; gift-card render emits neither slot and throws nothing; colour+size is one text node; no array shorthand in geometry; `audit:tokens` clean; `recipeGuards` confirms `Zimm*` namespacing on both recipes. |
564	| **3.1** | Drive the stepper through all five quantity conditions: 1, 2, at-max, fully-OOS, unavailable. Keyboard only: Tab to each control, Enter and Space. Confirm the focus ring is visibly different from rest. | Five states each assert the right enabled/disabled pair and the 0.4 opacity where greyed; keyboard operable; `aria-label` on both; focus-visible resolved value ≠ default; resolved target ≥24×24; `play` covers increment/decrement/boundary. |
565	| **3.2** | Render each of the three copy strings. Confirm DOM position between stepper and actions. Confirm error state widens the details gap. | Three strings verbatim; error → `status.error` token, warning → `text.muted` token; gap 12 → 16 on error; no hex literals; no low-stock variant in the union. |
566	| **3.3** | Render on-sale with quantity 2 and confirm both Was and Now scale. Render with and without a discount label. | Was struck, Now current, both quantity-scaled; label present only when the prop is; no `display-price` override created. |
567	| **3.4** | Feed the mapper a full line item, one with no image, one with missing colour, one with `c_maxOrderQuantity` absent, one with it set to 5, one with it set to `"abc"`. | Fallback returns 3 on absent/0/negative/non-numeric; returns 5 when set to 5; mapper emits one combined colour+size string; `grep` finds no SDK hook in any leaf; `product-detail/index.tsx` unmodified. |
568	| **3.6** (this row was still labeled 3.5 here after the 2026-09-18 renumbering — see the Commit order table and §4's own step heading, both correctly say 3.6; fixed 2026-09-19, found by the Tester dispatched for this exact step) | Run Storybook's a11y check on every story in B3. Then keyboard-only through a full cart item: image → name → price → stepper − → stepper + → message → Remove → Move to Wishlist. | 11 ACs each mapped in the PR body to a file and an assertion; a11y check green on every story; live region preserved (as of 2026-09-19, this step's own Scorer found the real mechanism is `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own `aria-live="polite"` value span, not `product-quantity-picker.tsx`'s now-orphaned `VisuallyHidden role="status"` — see §4's step 3.6 text); no colour-only state. |
569	| **4.1** | Mock passwordless success and assert the merge. Mock create-account and assert no merge. Then run the existing suites for `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu` and `product-view`. | `mergeBasket` once, `sum_quantities`, `createDestinationBasket: true`; not called on register; social route untouched; all four consumers' suites green; hook signature unchanged; blast radius named in the PR body. |

Make the server reject and confirm it stops. Drive the boundary at 2, 3, 4, 5. Then assert call **order**, not just end state. | One write under concurrency; one write per basket version; server rejection surfaces an error with no retry storm; `>=` boundary correct at 3 and 4; consolidation to one line at 3; merge → cap → resume order asserted; `useIsMutating()` no-op proven by making it fail on purpose first. |
571	| **4.3** | Emit each of the three messages. Confirm one emit site by grep. | One emit site; three strings verbatim; SFCC-404 marker present. The `within(document.body)`/portal-exception criterion is deferred to whichever of step 4.4/4.6 first renders a message-triggering component — see step 4.3's own pass criterion 3 text (corrected 2026-09-20) for why a hook-only step can't meet it. |
572	| **4.4** | Remove at qty 1 and qty 3. Wishlist-move at qty 1 and qty 3. Already-in-wishlist. Guest click. Guest completes email-code. Guest completes a simulated redirect. A 6-minute-old pending item. Keyboard-only on both links, checking the focus ring. | One call for a qty-3 remove (not three); single SKU saved on a qty-3 move; count decrements by full quantity; item stays in cart on already-in-wishlist and on guest click; resume works from state **and** from storage; stale item not resumed and both stores cleared; focus-visible ≠ default on both links. |
573	| **4.5** | Remove the last item. Confirm the discrete component renders and the header text changes at the same moment. Render at a non-AU site and inspect the CTA href. | Discrete component (no inline JSX); header and body both switch; CTA href site-prefixed; two-to-one collapse asserted; no hardcoded AU contact details. |
574	| **5.1** | Render domestic and count children. Render international and assert Apple Pay is absent from the DOM, then measure group height against domestic-minus-express. Drive hover/focus/active/disabled on all three buttons. Click Checkout domestic; click it as an international guest and as an international authenticated shopper. | Three children domestic in fixed order; **one** child international with `queryByRole` null and height unchanged; all five states asserted per button with focus-visible ≠ default; h52/px32/gap16 resolved from `actionSizes` tokens not literals; error story renders enabled with zero feedback copy; both international branches reach the stub; `countries.ts` unmodified. |
575	| **4.6** (inserted 2026-09-20, built after 5.1 — see its own step text for why the label doesn't match build order) | Render with a real multi-line basket and confirm one `ProductItem` per line via `cartItemMapper`'s own output. Force a basket over the cap and confirm the render guard fires exactly once and no-ops while a mutation is in flight. Click each item's Remove/Wishlist links and confirm the real mutations fire, not a stub. Render with zero items and confirm `ZimmCartEmptyState`, not an empty list. | One `ProductItem` per line, mapped not hand-built; render guard proven to run and to no-op under `useIsMutating()`, mirroring 4.2's own proof but for the real wiring; `secondaryActions` is a real `ZimmCartItemActions` on every item; empty state swaps in at zero items; `footer`/`messages` slots render `ZimmCartButtonGroup`/`useCartMessages` output; container owns no `isOpen`/`onClose` state itself; exactly one production `<ZimmCartDrawer` call site. |
576	
577	---
578	
579	## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)
580	
581	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
582	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
583	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
584	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
585	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
586	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
587	
588	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
589	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
590	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
591	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
592	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
593	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
594	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
595	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
596	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
597	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
598	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
599	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
600	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
601	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
602	3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
603	   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
604	   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
605	   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
606	   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
607	4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
608	   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
609	   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
610	   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
611	5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
612	   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
613	   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
614	   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
615	6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
616	   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
617	   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
618	   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
619	7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
620	   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
621	   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
622	   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
623	   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
624	8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
625	   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
626	   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
627	9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
628	   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
629	   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
630	   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
631	   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
632	   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
633	   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
634	   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
635	   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
636	   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
637	   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
638	   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
639	   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
640	   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about
641	   whether it renders *at all*, and no other gate in this loop checks for it.
642	
643	## 6. Open questions
644	
645	These block the handoff. None is a decision I should make for you.
646	
647	1. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 and owner approval is not confirmed.** B0 is BLOCKED until either the authenticated `gh` login is verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or a named approving review is secured. Until B0 lands, every cart PR gets `e2e_scope: skip` and no PR-time E2E.
648	
649	2. **`overrides/app/components/item-variant/` has no CODEOWNERS entry and there is no catch-all.** Five files with an 11-surface blast radius would merge with **no required reviewer**. Adding the entry is a Tier 1 Governance change to `CODEOWNERS`, explicitly outside my scope. Your call: add it as a separate ticket first, or accept that the widest-reaching part of this change is ungoverned and compensate with a manually-requested reviewer on B2.
650	
651	3. **`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` is also ungoverned, and the merge call changes auth behaviour for three surfaces outside the cart** (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`). Not in `frozenFiles.md`, not in `protectedFiles.md`'s shared-hooks list, no CODEOWNERS entry. This is a second instance of #2 and arguably the more dangerous one. Does B4 need an explicitly requested reviewer, and does the cross-surface behaviour change need Hard Rule #10 scope confirmation from you before it is written?
652	
653	4. **`overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist.** The settled decision says "use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not the base hook" — but that file is absent, and the path is listed in `protectedFiles.md` and routed in CODEOWNERS to `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. So honouring the decision literally means **creating a Tier 2 shared hook** this bundle has not budgeted a review for. My recommendation: import the base hook at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` and wrap it in our own untiered `useCartMessages.ts`. That satisfies the decision's actual intent (one handler, SFCC-404 is a one-file swap), costs no Tier 2 review, and automatically picks up the override the day someone creates it. I have **not** applied this — the decision is yours to confirm.
654	
655	5. **The stepper's `+` and `−` are a mismatched pair.** `MinusIcon` is a Zimmermann/Figma icon in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`; `PlusIcon` is re-exported from the base template in `index.tsx`. That file's own comments show the established pattern of migrating an icon into `zimm.tsx` when the base glyph is wrong (`CloseIcon`: "off-centre glyph within its viewBox"; the chevrons: filled vs stroked). AGENTS.md is explicit: if a required icon is missing from the overrides set, **ask — do not substitute a visually different one**. Is the base `PlusIcon` acceptable against Figma's `Icon_plus`, or does it need adding to `zimm.tsx`?
656	
657	6. **Apple Pay and Google Pay marks do not exist.** `zimm.tsx` has `ZimmAppleSignInIcon` and `ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` — sign-in marks, not Pay marks — and there is no `applePay`/`googlePay` asset anywhere in `overrides/app`. Both are brand-licensed artwork with usage rules. SFCC-275 AC1 requires 48×24 logos. Same AGENTS.md rule applies: ask, do not substitute. This is the only part of B5 that cannot pass.
658	
659	7. **Nothing opens the cart drawer, and no story owns the trigger.** See the closing line.
660	
661	8. **Container placement needs your confirmation.** SFCC-271's mutations and SFCC-250's guards need something that owns `useCurrentBasket()`, and `components.md` forbids data-fetching in anything under `overrides/app/components/`. Base `pages/cart/index.jsx` exists, so the override rule would normally say copy-first it — but the session notes decided 315 is explicitly "not an override of base `pages/cart`". My plan threads this by creating a **new custom file** at `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (a path CODEOWNERS already routes to `@pwa-squad-a`, Tier 3), leaving base `pages/cart/index.jsx` untouched and still serving `/cart` as today — a sibling file named anything other than `index` does not shadow the base page. Confirm that, or tell me to copy-first the page instead (which adds `index.jsx` + up to 13 partials to B2's scope).
662

## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)

Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about
   whether it renders *at all*, and no other gate in this loop checks for it.

## 6. Open questions

These block the handoff. None is a decision I should make for you.

1. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 and owner approval is not confirmed.** B0 is BLOCKED until either the authenticated `gh` login is verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or a named approving review is secured. Until B0 lands, every cart PR gets `e2e_scope: skip` and no PR-time E2E.

Does B4 need an explicitly requested reviewer, and does the cross-surface behaviour change need Hard Rule #10 scope confirmation from you before it is written?

My recommendation: import the base hook at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` and wrap it in our own untiered `useCartMessages.ts`. That satisfies the decision's actual intent (one handler, SFCC-404 is a one-file swap), costs no Tier 2 review, and automatically picks up the override the day someone creates it. 11. **SFCC-250 is not end-to-end verifiable this sprint.** Gate findings #1/#2: the TSD for SFCC-268 is `v0.1 Draft` with Technical Lead sign-off Pending, its own template says a TSD is not approved for implementation until signed, the live dev probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — and Jira nonetheless has SFCC-268 as Ready for SIT. import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the cart drawer's Checkout / Apple Pay / Google Pay button stack (SFCC-275, SFCC-11
 * plan step 5.1). Single style, no parts: all three buttons get their full visual treatment from
 * `ZimmButton`'s own `primary`/`secondary` recipe (`zimmButton.css.ts`) — this recipe only owns
 * the group's own layout, matching `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`'s single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` is `var(--zimm-size-action-gap)` (16px) — session-notes.md §11.5 confirms Figma's
 * `gap-[16px]` is literally `space/400`, and `foundation/sizes.ts`'s own comment on `actionSizes`
 * confirms this is the SAME action-sizing token `ZimmButton`'s own `lg` size (h52/px32) already
 * resolves through, not a second, independently-typed 16px value.
 *
 * No fixed `height`/`minHeight` here, deliberately — SFCC-11 plan step 5.1 AC2 ("no white gap"
 * when the international variant renders one child instead of three): a plain flexbox `gap`
 * naturally removes both a removed child's own height AND its adjacent gap when that child is
 * gone, with nothing here to compensate. Adding a fixed height would silently reintroduce exactly
 * the dead-space bug AC2 exists to prevent — see this recipe's own `index.test.tsx` assertion
 * that no `height`/`minHeight` key exists on this baseStyle.
 */
export const ZimmCartButtonGroup = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    width: '100%',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-size-action-gap)',
  },
});

2	import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
3	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
4	import { MultiSiteProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
5	import { ZimmCartButtonGroup } from '.';
6	
7	// Real generated site/locale pairs (overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts) — useCountryConfig
8	// matches on BOTH sfccSiteId and locale, and silently falls back to AU on any mismatch, so getting
9	// these exactly right matters for the International story to actually exercise checkoutOwner
10	// 'global-e' rather than quietly rendering the domestic layout instead.
11	const AU_SITE = { id: 'ZimmermannAU', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannAU' };
12	const AU_LOCALE = { id: 'en' };
13	const HK_SITE = { id: 'ZimmermannHK', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannHK' };
14	const HK_LOCALE = { id: 'en-HK' };
15	
16	const meta: Meta<typeof ZimmCartButtonGroup> = {
17	  title: 'Commerce/ZimmCartButtonGroup',
18	  component: ZimmCartButtonGroup,
19	  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
20	};
21	
22	export default meta;
23	
24	type Story = StoryObj<typeof ZimmCartButtonGroup>;
25	
26	/** Domestic (AU, checkoutOwner 'sfcc') — all three buttons in fixed order (AC1). */
27	export const Default: Story = {
28	  decorators: [
29	    (Story) => (
30	      <MemoryRouter>
31	        <MultiSiteProvider site={AU_SITE} locale={AU_LOCALE} buildUrl={(path: string) => path}>
32	          <Story />
33	        </MultiSiteProvider>
34	      </MemoryRouter>
35	    ),
36	  ],
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * International (HK, checkoutOwner 'global-e') — express buttons removed, not hidden (AC2): only
41	 * the Checkout button renders, with no compensating gap/height left behind.
42	 */
43	export const International: Story = {
44	  decorators: [
45	    (Story) => (
46	      <MemoryRouter>
47	        <MultiSiteProvider site={HK_SITE} locale={HK_LOCALE} buildUrl={(path: string) => path}>
48	          <Story />
49	        </MultiSiteProvider>
50	      </MemoryRouter>
51	    ),
52	  ],
53	};
54	
55	/**
56	 * SFCC-275 ACs 3/4 — a shopper's cart has a blocking error (e.g. a max-quantity-reached inline
57	 * message elsewhere in the drawer), but all three buttons still render enabled with no feedback
58	 * copy of their own: this component takes no error-related prop at all, so this story is
59	 * intentionally identical to Default — the point being demonstrated is the *absence* of any
60	 * error-driven disabling, not a distinct visual state. See index.test.tsx for the assertion that
61	 * backs this up mechanically rather than by inspection alone.
62	 */
63	export const ErrorInCart: Story = {
64	  decorators: [
65	    (Story) => (
66	      <MemoryRouter>
67	        <MultiSiteProvider site={AU_SITE} locale={AU_LOCALE} buildUrl={(path: string) => path}>
68	          <Story />
69	        </MultiSiteProvider>
70	      </MemoryRouter>
71	    ),
72	  ],
73	};

# INTERNATIONAL STOREFRONT — no Apple Pay / Google Pay

3 nodes: `9323:65941` (`cart/drawer/large`, 1440px, panel 1186px — pulled in full), `9323:66038`
(tablet — not independently pulled this pass), `9323:66119` (`cart/drawer/mobile`, 402px —
pulled in full).

## Confirms `plan.md`'s SFCC-275 build rationale exactly, via live pull

The `Button-group` container has **exactly one child** at both breakpoints checked — a single
`Button` div with "CHECKOUT" text, `bg-[var(--alias/color/action/primary/bg/default,#191919)]`.
No Apple Pay / Google Pay `Button` divs or logo instances exist anywhere in either node's tree —
genuinely absent from the component structure, not hidden via opacity/visibility/conditional
render. This directly confirms the plan's own claim ("the Figma Button-group has exactly one
child... a plain conditional render with nothing to compensate for").

## New, not previously logged: a duties/taxes disclosure line

Beneath the button group, above the (absent, in this group) promo-code accordion:
> "Duties and taxes are included in the price displayed"

`text.subtle` (`#666`), 14px, Futura Round regular/400, lineHeight 18px, full width. Present at
both large and mobile. **Not mentioned anywhere in `plan.md`'s SFCC-275 section** — worth
checking in the later code-comparison pass whether this copy exists anywhere in the cart
totals/button-group area already, or whether it's a genuinely new, unbuilt requirement specific
to international storefronts.

## Real breakpoint inconsistency, flagged not resolved

At the **mobile** breakpoint (`9323:66119`) only, the Checkout button is `h-[40px]`
`px-[var(--alias/space/500,20px)]` — smaller than the `h-[52px]` / `px-[32px]` (space/800) used
for the same button at large, and used for every button in every other group pulled in this
audit (`default-page-template.md`, `cart-merge.md`). `plan.md`'s own SFCC-275 spec states
"h52/px32/min-w80/w-full" uniformly with no mobile exception. This may be a deliberate
mobile-compact sizing choice or a Figma-file inconsistency — recorded precisely for Marcel/the
designer to adjudicate, not resolved here. Not yet checked against the actual shipped
`ZimmCartButtonGroup` (not yet built — this is step 5.1, still ahead in the plan) since there is
no code yet to compare against for this specific component.

Not otherwise checked against shipped code — this pass is Figma-only, and SFCC-275 hasn't been
built yet regardless.

## Verdict: PASS

Step 5.1 (`ZimmCartButtonGroup`) ships as-is. Working tree confirmed to be exactly the declared manifest (4 modified + 2 new SVG + 1 new component folder) — nothing else touched.

| Axis | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | PASS, with one out-of-scope gap flagged below (not scored against this step) | Live Chromium render against the running `localhost:6006` (fresh screenshots + computed styles, not jsdom, not a source read) |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS — 9/9 | Independently reproduced most, not just relayed |
| **Correctness** | PASS | `tsc` clean; `npm run test` 123 files/1704 tests green; lint 0 errors; `audit:tokens` clean for touched files |
| **Conformance** | PASS | `recipeGuards`/`recipeParts`/`theme/index` tests green; token chain traced to source |
| **Completeness** | PASS | Story + test present, ACs covered with evidence |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Diff = exactly the declared manifest; `hideLabelVisually` is a disclosed, additive, backward-compatible atom change |

### What I tried to falsify

1. **The SVG "verbatim copy" claim** — wrote a script (not eyeballing) that extracted every `d="..."` from the committed `.svg` files and from the inlined JSX and diffed them structurally. Both Apple (1 path) and Google (4 paths) matched **byte-for-byte**. Survived.
2. **"Non-distorted Google Pay mark"** — the single highest-risk visual claim in the brief. Rendered the `Default` story in real Chromium and measured the actual painted `<svg>` bounding box: Apple = 48×24 (viewBox 0 0 48 24, exact match); Google = 45×18 (viewBox 0 0 45.1717 18 → aspect 2.510 vs rendered aspect 2.500, a 0.4% rounding artefact from the plan's own disclosed `45.1717→45` rounding, not stretching to the 48×24 slot). Confirmed visually too — the "G Pay" mark's circle reads round, not squashed. Survived.
3. **"Icon-only, label present but invisible"** — live `getComputedStyle` on the actual painted label spans: "Checkout" is `position: static`, genuinely visible; "Apple Pay"/"Google Pay" are `position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden` — the real sr-only clip, in a real browser, not jsdom. Screenshot confirms nothing but the two logos is visible. Survived.
4. **The token-derivation chain** (not just "a var name looks token-like") — traced `h52`/`px32`/`gap16` from the test assertion → `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `sizes.lg` → `zimmTokens.ts` → `foundation/sizes.ts`'s `actionSizes`, confirming `52px`/`32px`/`16px` are typed **once**, not re-typed at each layer. Live-measured the rendered boxes too: button height 52px, padding 32px, group height 188px = exactly `3×52 + 2×16`. Survived.
5. **AC2 ("no compensating gap")** — live-rendered `International`: exactly one button, 52px total height (identical to the domestic Checkout button's own height, not stretched). Survived.
6. **Focus-visible ≠ default (WCAG 2.4.7)** — live: default outline `rgba(0,0,0,0) solid 2px` (invisible) vs focused `rgb(25,25,25) solid 1px` (real, visible) — `outlinesDiffer: true`, corroborated by an existing screenshot from earlier today showing a clearly visible ring on the Apple Pay button.
7. **The "9 non-null-assertion comments" fix didn't disturb anything** — grepped all 9 `Button.variants!`/`Button.sizes!` sites, confirmed each carries the justifying comment (word-for-word identical to two sibling files' established pattern), re-ran the full suite: still 1704/1704 green, `tsc` clean.
8. **Pulled the project's own pre-build Figma audit (`discrepancies.md`, 2026-09-19) rather than trusting plan.md's step 5.1 text alone** — this is what surfaced the one real gap below.

Nothing I attacked broke. This was not a rubber-stamp — item 8 in particular took the review somewhere the brief didn't point me.

### What I could not verify

- **Real `:hover` CSS matching.** Playwright's `.hover()` hung on an unrelated element after a self-inflicted contamination (I'd briefly copied a temp script into the tracked project root, which Storybook's file-watcher picked up as an HMR trigger, invalidating my page mid-script — cleaned up immediately, `git status` confirms no trace). My replacement (dispatching a synthetic `MouseEvent`) doesn't hit-test the way a real pointer does, so `_hover` background-swap is confirmed only via the recipe source + unit test (`_hover.bg !== bg`), not a live repaint. Already covered by the Tester's own live pass per the brief — not re-verified independently by me.
- **Active/disabled states** — confirmed via source/unit-test cross-check only, not live-driven by me this pass (already in the Tester's stated scope).
- **The live Figma file itself** — I had no working Figma-tool access in this session; my Design-fidelity cross-check against Figma used this project's own committed audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`, dated 2026-09-19, i.e. 2 days before this build), not a fresh pull. Treat the finding below as PLAUSIBLE off that document, not CONFIRMED off a live Figma read today.

### Defects

None REWORK-worthy. No `file:line` instruction to give.

### Residual risk (shipping this step)

`checkoutOwner: 'hybrid'` (US) renders all three buttons, same as domestic — already disclosed as a deliberate, unresolved product-decision gap (`countries.ts`'s own doc comment implies hybrid should sometimes behave like `global-e`, and no per-shopper shipping signal exists yet to do that). Shipping now means every US shopper sees Apple Pay/Google Pay unconditionally until that product decision lands — small blast radius, but it's a live shopper-facing behaviour going out on an inference, not a sign-off.

### Marcel visual checkpoint — owed, here's what it should show

Storybook running locally, three URLs:

1. **`http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--default`** — black "CHECKOUT" button, then two white bordered buttons showing the **Apple Pay** and **Google Pay** logo lockups only (no separate "Apple Pay"/"Google Pay" caption text next to the mark — the wordmark IS the mark). All three full-width, same height, 16px gaps. The Google Pay "G" should read as a round circle, not an oval — that's the distortion check.
2. **`.../story/commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--international`** — only the black "CHECKOUT" button, full stop. No blank space where the other two used to be.
3. **`.../story/commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--error-in-cart`** — identical to Default, all three enabled, no error text anywhere in the group (that absence is the point of this story).

Something's wrong if: any visible "Apple Pay"/"Google Pay" caption appears next to the logos; the Google Pay mark looks horizontally or vertically stretched; International shows dead space below Checkout; any button's Tab-focus doesn't produce a visible ring.

### What Marcel is missing

This project's own pre-build Figma audit (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/figma-reference/international-storefront.md`, written 2026-09-19 — 2 days before this step was built) flagged two facts about the international button-group frame that never made it into plan.md's step 5.1 text and aren't owned by any step in the current 20-commit manifest: (1) a **"Duties and taxes are included in the price displayed" disclosure line**, positioned beneath the button group and above a promo-code accordion that also doesn't exist yet in this build — real Figma copy, currently unbuilt, currently unowned; (2) a **mobile-breakpoint Checkout button** in Figma sized `h40/px20` against the `h52/px32` used everywhere else, flagged in that doc as "needs a design call... not resolved here." I'm not scoring either against this step — the first is architecturally a drawer/organism-level element, not this molecule's job, and building it unasked would itself be a Restraint violation; the second was implicitly superseded by plan.md's own explicit uniform-sizing spec, which is a defensible call given the audit itself called it possibly "a Figma-file inconsistency." But nobody has explicitly picked either up, and the international drawer will ship without that disclosure line unless someone assigns it to a step.

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/{index.test.tsx,index.stories.tsx,zimmCartButtonGroup.css.ts}`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/assets/svg/{apple-pay-logo.svg,google-pay-logo.svg}`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/{index.tsx,index.test.tsx,index.stories.tsx}`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md` (step 5.1, lines 480-509; §5.0 Verification standard, lines 579-641)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/HANDOFF.md` (lines 386-408, the two disclosed non-scope findings)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/figma-reference/international-storefront.md` (the disclosure-line/breakpoint gap cited above)
